analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and a changelog: changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md (added) and docs/architecture/inference.md (hunks at head lines ~810-813, ~829, ~1896-1899). No executable code is visible, so no direct security regression can be shown from these units.

The docs describe two behavior changes that the source diffs, which are not in this batch, must implement. (1) GLM-5.3-Flash now accepts variable-frame-rate video. Frames are indexed in presentation order and frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, then the unchanged 2 FPS sampler runs. The documented 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token cap and the processor's video duration and frame limits must still bound work for VFR clips. A VFR track's real frame count can differ from duration times the nominal rate, so a mismatch could weaken the pixel and duration bounds. This is relevant to the availability and memory exposure of provider media decoding (TB-003, TB-007, ADV-002). (2) The shared media path (GLM, Gemma, Qwen) now admits the data:video/mov and data:video/x-m4v labels. The docs say the label only gates the part and that MemoryBackedVideoAsset sniffs MP4 or QuickTime from the bytes. That keeps the container check content-based, but I could not verify the code, so the next pass should confirm that the admitted-header list and the byte sniff behave as described, and that Nemotron's separate label list is unchanged as claimed.

T-041 and the prefix-cache findings are not touched. The docs say media requests stay excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so cache and TTFT exposure is unchanged. Whether the 25 MiB inline cap, 600 s duration cap and 384 Mpx request cap are still enforced for VFR clips and the new labels in MediaIngest and GLM5NextProcessor cannot be confirmed from this batch. No findings; the code changes need review elsewhere.
